Modern table formats like Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, and Apache Hudi provide features such as ACID transactions, schema evolution, and time travel capabilities for large-scale data management. Table formats serve as the foundational layer between raw storage and data processing engines. * File organization and naming conventions * Transaction handling and concurrency control * Data versioning and time travel capabilities Unlike traditional file formats (CSV, Parquet), table formats provide a higher-level abstraction that ensures data consistency and reliability across distributed systems. results.title: So you want Database Versioning? | DoltHub Blog
results.content: # So you want Database Versioning? Dolt is a version controlled database, a Git database, Git for data, data version control, an immutable database, and a decentralized database. Dolt can also be used for database versioning. # What is Database Versioning?#. ## Versioning#. Database versioning is applying forks, branches, diffs, merges, and conflicts to a database, preferably in a decentralized way. But how would you apply versioning to a database? For the purposes of versioning, a database can be thought of as two separate concepts: schema and data. Until recently, database schema was all you could version. I had never heard versioning schema called database versioning or database version control until recently. The term I heard for for version controlling database schema was database migration. But, a number of databases are designed this way to give versioning features to their applications. # Why version your database?#. Database versioning minimizes downtime caused by database changes. Database versioning allows you to roll back bad changes quickly. Database versioning improves developer productivity. Database versioning allows you to share your database between development, staging, and production. Moreover, if there is a bug in production involving the database, a developer can reproduce the bug locally using database versioning. Restore the database to the version where the error is occurring, attach a debugger to your application, and reproduce the bug. Finally, database versioning allows you to create versioned applications. Traditionally, as noted above, adding versioning to databases for applications uses a technique called Slowly Changing Dimension. Modern version controlled databases can replace slowly changing dimension, simplify your application code, grant the additional ability to render diffs, and give you the database versioning benefits above. # Database Versioning Options#. We broke the tools down into three categories: Database Migration Tools, Versioned Data Lakes, and Version Controlled Databases. ## Version Controlled Databases#. TerminusDB has full schema and data versioning capability but offers a graph database interface using a custom query language called Web Object Query Language (WOQL). If you think your database version control makes more sense in graph or document form, check them out. We’re a little biased but we think adding branch and merge to a SQL database in a decentralized way is true database versioning.

results.title: Term entity type's "parent" field is now a standard Entity ... - Drupal
results.content: Published Time: 2018-01-19T21:48:52+00:00 Term entity type's "parent" field is now a standard Entity Reference field and the taxonomy_term_hierarchy table has been removed | Drupal.org Skip to main contentSkip to search Can we use first and third party cookies and web beacons to understand our audience, and to tailor promotions you see? Yes, please No, do not track me * Sign up for Drupal News * : Log in, view profile, and more Learn how to support DDEV Term entity type's "parent" field is now a standard Entity Reference field and the taxonomy_term_hierarchy table has been removed By wim leers on 19 January 2018 Published (View all published change records) With entity reference fields, you can do: $term->parent->target_id // returns always NULL, even if the term has a parent This field has always been a special case, because it is marked as , so its values are never loaded. REST support is missing: it's impossible to access a term's parent term via core's Serialization module, core's REST module, contrib's JSON API module, contrib's GraphQL module or contrib's Default Content module 2. Migrate D8 source support would need to be custom. See #2935951: Copy migrate source plugin from migrate_drupal_d8 into migrate_drupal") To fix all of them at the root, rather than adding more custom code and work-arounds, we changed to not use custom field storage for its This also allowed custom code to be deleted. It strengthens Drupal 8's Entity API: more things work in a predictable way. ### DB schema change The move from custom storage to non-custom storage means that the Taxonomy module no longer needs to define a custom schema: the table (manually created by the Taxonomy module) disappears in favor of an auto-created table (automatically created by the field system). Per this is not a BC break: > While the database query API and schema API itself are stable, the schema of any particular table is not. Code using the Entity Query API does not need to be updated. Custom SQL queries using the table will need to be updated, and are recommended to use the Entity Query API instead. ### Impact on Views All views continue to work, there is an automated update path for them to use the new auto-created table.

results.title: How should a data scientist handle versioning, both for pipeline code and models? - Quora
results.content: How should a data scientist handle versioning, both for pipeline code and models? Besides code, data scientists also need to version control a few more things. Besides code, data scientists also need to version control a few more things. But the code and data for producing other models need to be version controlled. Versioning for data science must treat code, data, and models as first‑class artifacts and use practices that make experiments reproducible, traceable, and deployable. * Traceability: every model version must link to the exact code commit, dataset snapshot (or data query. Versioning for data science must treat code, data, and models as first‑class artifacts and use practices that make experiments reproducible, traceable, and deployable. * Traceability: every model version must link to the exact code commit, dataset snapshot (or data query), training config, random seeds, and environment spec. Within a mature pipeline, every production prediction references a model version that can be traced back to exact code, data, and environment.
